intro: You are standing before Yedikule Fortress, a castle and walls in İstanbul province, dating from 1458. Mehmed II grafted this seven-towered fortress onto the Golden Gate of the Theodosian walls. It served as treasury, as arsenal, and as the state prison where envoys were held.
history: In 1458 Mehmed II added three towers to the Golden Gate section of the Theodosian walls. Together with the four already there, they made a fortress of seven towers. It served first as treasury and arsenal, and then became the state prison. When a state went to war with the Ottomans, its ambassadors were held here. And in 1622, Osman II was killed within these walls.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Golden Gate, the seven towers, the prison chambers and the inscribed walls.
facts: Did you know? The scratchings prisoners left on the cell walls can still be read: names and dates in Latin, Greek, French and Russian. Imagine the long days behind every line. And the fortress itself was made in 1458 by adding three towers to the Golden Gate of the Theodosian walls; with the four already there, the count reached seven.
outro: This brings our tour of Yedikule Fortress to an end. Please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. Thank you for listening, and enjoy your visit.
